segments.narration: Entire desert dunes suddenly start humming like a pipe organ. Marco Polo heard them back in the thirteenth century.
Marco Polo wrote about phantom instruments playing across the Gobi Desert. Explorers blamed evil spirits or underground bells.
For centuries, no one could explain why barren sand traps would roar like low-flying aircraft. Could wind alone create a concert?
Physicists finally solved the puzzle using high-speed cameras. Friction between rolling quartz grains creates a synchronized acoustic wave.
The exact frequency depends on grain size and moisture levels. Can you imagine hearing an entire mountain hum?
